title: Eul Alternative for macOS | Better Resource Monitor
description: Compare Eul and Better Resource Monitor for macOS. Keep CPU, memory, storage, GPU, and network visible with active support and low overhead.
heading: Better Resource Monitor vs Eul
intro: A lot of people liked Eul because it was small, simple, and easy to keep in the menu bar. Better Resource Monitor aims for that same kind of everyday usefulness, but with active maintenance, support for current Macs, and lower overhead on Apple Silicon.

sections.heading: Why people move on from Eul
sections.body: Eul still has a nice, minimal feel, but it is no longer being actively maintained. That matters more for a system monitor than it does for most apps, because macOS keeps changing the APIs and hardware details these tools depend on.

sections.heading: Better fit for newer Macs
sections.body: On Apple Silicon, Better Resource Monitor stays under 0.1% CPU and uses about 15 MB of memory. That makes it easier to leave running all day, which is the whole point of a menu bar monitor in the first place.

sections.heading: Technical choices, practical result
sections.body: Better Resource Monitor uses public APIs for GPU data, stays sandboxed, and is available on the Mac App Store with full features. Those are technical details, but the practical result is simple: a monitor that is easier to install, easier to trust, and less likely to break on the next macOS update.

cta: If you liked Eul's simpler style but want something current, [Better Resource Monitor is on the Mac App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/better-resource-monitor/id6758237306) and covers the same everyday use case. The source is on [GitHub](https://github.com/alexx855/better-resource-monitor) if you want to look before you install.
